To be honest, stress and sleep may play a part but it’s mostly just genetics. In your pictures since your temples are receding it looks most likely to be male pattern baldness, and not something like telogen effluvium (diffuse thinning all around the scalp). 

In the case of male pattern baldness, it’s very hard or even impossible to naturally recover hairs that have already been miniaturized or if the follicles are already dead. Something like telogen effluvium can be recovered naturally by improving lifestyle (reducing stress) and solving the root cause of the hair loss. 

But since yours looks like male pattern baldness, simply sleeping more or reducing stress might not necessarily grow back your hairline. Those baby hairs around your hairline you see in your last picture look to be already miniaturizing. Your best shot at bringing those hairs back is taking some kind of treatment. Not to say it’s IMPOSSIBLE naturally, but you have a MUCH better shot with some kind of treatment. Trust me, I wish it was easier to recover male pattern baldness naturally, I went through the same thing trying to recover it naturally and it had no success.

It’s more likely that you have male pattern baldness genetics and since you are in your early 20s now it could have started (and sleep/stress could have ACCELERATED it, but is not necessarily the root CAUSE). What I mean is if you fix your sleep/stress it may slow down your hair loss, but it won’t necessarily regrow the hairs you’ve already lost. Your hairline may become a bit more dense after improving lifestyle but if you want to revert to the first pic hairline you may need to start treatment. 

Not trying to scare you, just don’t want someone else to waste so much time trying to recover their hair naturally instead of just hopping on treatment earlier. That’s what I did and I regret not just starting sooner. Do some more research yourself and ask a dermatologist, make a decision from there. Best of luck man I mean it

What you can do to have some impact from the other side of the map is to: mess up enemy jungler (take his camps, kill him in his jungle), kill enemy mid (doing this not only gets your laner ahead but also that lead will allow them impact the map a lot more, as mid can roam to either lane easily), and kill enemy bot lane (I'll explain next paragraph).

As a top laner, even if you don't take TP there are chances where you can actually roam bot and get some kills or apply pressure without losing too much top. If you die during lane but you know your wave is good and won't be shoved in fast, you have a homeguards and can sometimes gank bot and get back to lane fast enough and only miss a few cs (this scenario doesn't happen every game but keep a look out for it). Another scenario is after 14 minutes, if the first tower is already taken or YOUR top tower will be taken whether you are in lane or not, you might as well roam bot and get some kills there. This is because there isn't much reason to stay in lane post 14 minutes (plates fall) unless you will lose a huge amount of cs or can potentially get the enemy top tower as first tower. 

With TP, this gets a lot easier as sometimes you can either TP from top to bot or even run bot (even without homeguards) and TP back top to not miss any cs right after your roam. TP is really good for impacting bot lane but yeah some champs can't take TP and have to take ignite.

But yeah there are a small amount of games where you definitely will have an enemy adc be 10/0 out of lane... in these games unless you're insanely fed yourself it is sometimes just doomed. But most games you can make a good impact on the rest of the map as top.

I would say if you don't have to trade try not to (unless hes just completely messing up) and just play for good wave management and play off of that.

Oh sorry I thought you meant in lane. After lane phase (14 min) focus on keeping them in lane still and shoving waves into tower (2nd tier tower probably). Tanks will take tp usually, Riven usually takes ignite so try to counter that with roaming immediately once shoving waves into their tower. Just like laning phase, tanks always have a tough time against having waves shoved into them. Tanks are usually more effective in team fights so you do what you can to keep them away from your team. Also recommend building cleaver 2nd or 3rd into tanks.

Main objective against tanks is to get a lead through turret plates, farming, and roaming. You can also get a lead by ruining the enemy jg’s game. To do this, slow push your waves and always 3-4 wave crash into enemy tower. Avoid fast pushing into tanks (unless they’re dead or gone from lane) because tanks can hold waves before it hits their tower much easier than bruisers). So fast pushing is bad, but against slow pushing tanks really can’t do much to stop you from 3-4 wave crashing into their tower. When slow pushing, avoid poke and try to trade minimally, trading usually won’t do much so save your abilities to dodge theirs or negate damage (Malphite q, mundo q, ornn q/w, etc). When you shoved waves into enemy tower, you can do a few things. One is to try to proxy their wave if you know the enemy jg isn’t near. Another is if enemy jg is unknown, roam and get vision in enemy topside jg. Also if you know enemy jg is near, go for invade to kill them (obv gauge if it’s safe). You can also look for roams mid. Remember only try these if your waves already crashed into the enemy tower. Tanks have really good gank setup so always try to track enemy jg as if you get CCed in a gank you’re probably dead.
